findings.title: Backup-code sign-in can bypass password/first-factor verification
findings.body: In the CredentialsProvider authorize function, the password is verified only when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121). The backup-code path at line 131 is taken whenever `credentials.backupCode` is present. A caller can therefore POST credentials containing a valid `backupCode` and an arbitrary non-empty `totpCode`; the password check is skipped and the backup code alone authenticates the user. For password accounts this removes the password factor, and for non-CAL identity-provider accounts it also bypasses the OAuth/SAML first factor. Consequence: account takeover if a backup code is known or leaked.

findings.title: Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write
findings.body: After decrypting `user.backupCodes`, the code sets the used entry to null and writes the whole encrypted array back. Two parallel successful logins can read the same array before either update completes; one update can overwrite the other, restoring an already-used code, or the same code can be accepted by both requests. One-time backup codes are therefore not guaranteed to be single-use. Use a transaction/row lock or an atomic consumption mechanism.

findings.title: Backup codes are compared case-sensitively and without trimming
findings.body: The server only removes dashes before doing `indexOf`. Generated codes are lowercase hex, while the UI placeholder uses uppercase. If a user types or pastes uppercase letters, leading/trailing whitespace, or other formatting, the comparison fails even for a valid code. Normalize by trimming, removing separators, and lowercasing before comparison. The same issue exists in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`.

findings.title: Modal state reset does not clear react-hook-form/TOTP value
findings.body: `resetState` only clears password, error, and step; it does not call `form.reset()` or clear the registered `totpCode`. Because the component auto-submits when `totpCode?.trim().length === 6` (line 157), a stale six-digit value left from a previous enable attempt can trigger an unintended enable request or surface errors when the modal is reopened. It also leaves secret/backup-code state and object URLs in memory.

findings.title: 2FA enable success is not propagated if backup-code dialog is dismissed
findings.body: After `handleEnable` succeeds, the modal moves to the backup-code step and calls `onEnable` only from the explicit Close button. If the user closes the dialog with Escape/overlay/close affordance, `onOpenChange` closes the modal without calling `onEnable`, even though 2FA has already been enabled server-side. The settings UI can remain in the disabled/stale state until a refresh.

findings.title: Blob object URL for backup-code download is not revoked on close/unmount
findings.body: `URL.createObjectURL` is called during setup, but the URL is only revoked if setup runs again. Closing the modal or unmounting the component leaves the blob URL alive, causing a small memory leak. Revoke the URL in a cleanup effect or when the modal closes.

findings.title: No e2e coverage for the new backup-code login/disable paths
findings.body: The PR adds UI for backup codes and server-side consumption, but the tests only verify that the codes are displayed/copied/downloaded. The TODO acknowledges missing tests for logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code. Without coverage, the critical backup-code authentication/consumption logic can regress unnoticed.

findings.title: Password visibility toggle is removed from keyboard focus
findings.body: Adding `tabIndex={-1}` to the show/hide password button prevents keyboard users from focusing and activating it. This makes the password field less accessible; the control should remain focusable or provide an equivalent keyboard-accessible alternative.

findings.title: Backup code input is assumed to be a string
findings.body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll` is called without validating the body field type. A malformed POST with a number/object/array for `backupCode` will throw a TypeError and return a 500 instead of a validation error. Validate/sanitize the field as a string before processing; the same assumption exists in the NextAuth credentials handler.

findings.title: Submitting an empty backup-code form can fail silently
findings.body: The login form has `noValidate`, so the BackupCode input's required/minLength attributes are not enforced. If a user is on the lost-access screen and submits an empty backup code, the server falls back to the TOTP branch and returns `second-factor-required`; the client merely keeps the two-factor screen and displays no error, leaving the user stuck. Show an error or validate the backup code client-side before submitting.
